Question: Let \(f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}\) be defined by \(f(z) = z^2 + iz + 1.\) How many complex numbers \(z\) are there such that \(\operatorname{Im}(z) \gt 0\) and both the real and the imaginary parts of \(f(z)\) are integers with absolute value at most \(10?\)
